# Introduction

The API is a REST based API with OAuth2 authentication and enables you to
either access your own account via programmable software, or access data
from foreign accounts that have given you the explicit permission to do so.

You can access the API from any programming language that supports basic HTTP-Requests and can interact with the JSON data format.

To be able to use the API you need to have a registered account
(also if you are a 3rd-party softwareprovider and not using the application yourself).

# Quickstart

Our Pingen Quick Start Guide helps you get up and running with Pingen API in just a few steps.

### Register a user and create an organisation

In order to use Pingen API, you need to create a Pingen account. To do so, go to the Pingen identity sign-up page and enter your email address.

You can select from two environments:
 * For the production environment, use [https://identity.pingen.com/auth/register](https://identity.pingen.com/auth/register)
 * For the testing/staging environment, use [https://identity-staging.pingen.com/auth/register](https://identity-staging.pingen.com/auth/register)

The testing/staging environment is a 1:1 copy of the production environment however no letters are printed or sent. Instead, you can simulate the behavior of printed letters based on the file name ([see here](#section/Simulation))

### OAuth grant type

The Pingen API uses OAuth2 for authorisation. When creating a Developer-App, you receive a Client- ID and a Client-Secret.
These are required during authentication and when generating the API Access Token.
 * Decide on your OAuth grant type (probably Client Credentials, see [here](#section/Authentication/Which-grant-type-should-i-use))
 * Obtain your OAuth credentials ([see here](#section/Authentication/How-to-obtain-a-Client-ID))

### API usage

 * If available, [use one of our SDKs](#section/Basics/SDK) to send your first letter (you can stop here)
 * If you will not use an SDK:
1) Obtain your first access token ([see here](#section/Authentication/Use-Client-credentials-grant))
2) Send your first letter by examining our [curl examples](#operation/letters.create) (on the right hand side) for sending a letter

### Postman collection

Another great way to better understanding of how to form API requests and how to make API calls is to use a powerful application called Postman.
It is an API platform for developers to form and test their API calls. This highly popular tool is easy to use, offers web and desktop apps and you can sign up and get started with Postman for free.

What makes it even better is that you can use a collection of our ready-made Pingen API services and explore them in more detail.
Using Postman, you can easily manipulate parameters, environments, etc. Thus, it makes testing of API services almost effortless.

You can find a Pingen API collection [here](https://www.postman.com/pingen/workspace/pingen-v2-public-workspace)

### More information

Before you go live with your integration, we highly recommend you to read our [Basics](#section/Basics) section

# Basics

Following is important information about how in general you interact with the API as well as what to look out for while implementing it.

## FAQ

### What is the easiest way to connect my software to Pingen?
Integrating the API is only necessary for more complicated workflows or when delivering letters of third party clients. If you are planning to simply deliver your PDFs for automatic dispatching and delivery, you can also opt for a much simpler Integration for example with an S3-Bucket where you deliver, and we fetch the PDFs.

### Do you have a Sandbox environment?
Yes. Our Sandbox is called Staging and is a fully separate environment where you need to [register a separate account](https://identity-staging.pingen.com/auth/register) and create separate API credentials.

### What is auto_send when creating a letter?
When [creating a letter](#operation/letters.create) you can specify that it is automatically submitted for sending when we have finished analysing and processing it. This is by far the simplest way to push a letter.

### What are 'virtual' delivery products (fast, cheap, bulk etc)
Virtual delivery products work for a letter which is sent into any country. We automatically choose the most appropriate delivery product so you do not have to worry about mapping available delivery products to countries.

### Why are several fields in response empty after creating a letter?
After creating a letter we process it asynchronously and depending on the system load, this can take from a few milliseconds to several minutes. We suggest you use [webhooks](#operation/misc.webhooks) to receive all the details of a letter after it has been sent.

### Can I upload several letters at once?
When sending individual letters (one PDF per letter) you have to do separate API calls for each letter. If you are uploading a ZIP-File or Merged-PDF you should use [batches](#operation/batches.create).

### Should i continously poll the API to get status updates?
No this is not recommended. We highly recommend you use [webhooks](#operation/misc.webhooks) instead.

### Where is the list of all statuses and event codes?
We do not provide a complete list of statuses or event codes. Use [webhooks](#operation/misc.webhooks) to be notified of lifecycle changes in a letter.

## SDK

### Java SDK

Use [our official Java SDK](https://github.com/pingencom/pingen2-sdk-java)

### PHP SDK

Use [our official PHP SDK](https://github.com/pingencom/pingen2-sdk-php)

### Python SDK

Use [our official Python SDK](https://github.com/pingencom/pingen2-sdk-python)

### Js SDK

Use [our official Js SDK](https://github.com/pingencom/pingen2-sdk-js)

### Go SDK

Use [our official Go SDK](https://github.com/pingencom/pingen2-sdk-go)

### Rust SDK

Use [our official Rust SDK](https://github.com/pingencom/pingen2-sdk-rust)

### .NET SDK (Third-Party)

One of our trusted clients has created a [third-party .NET SDK](https://github.com/AMANDA-Technology/PingenApiNet)

### All Other languages

For any other language there is currently no official or third-party SDK available. Please look at our CURL examples or implement the raw HTTP calls directly. If you have developed an SDK for a project and are maintaining the code, please contact our support to be listed here.

## Environments

All URLs referred to in this documentation are relative and have to be used in combination with the API or IDENTITY URL which there are following available:

### Production

URL | Description
----------- | --------
https://api.pingen.com | Resource API. Used to interact with collections and objects.
https://identity.pingen.com | Identity management & authentication. Used for issuing access tokens, login, password reset etc.

### Staging

 **IMPORTANT:** Staging is a fully separate environment. You need to [register a user](https://identity-staging.pingen.com/auth/register) and create Client-IDs for staging in order to interact with that environment.

URL | Description
----------- | --------
https://api-staging.pingen.com | Resource API. Used to interact with collections and objects.
https://identity-staging.pingen.com | Identity management & authentication. Used for issuing access tokens, login, password reset etc.

The interaction format (input and output) for nearly all endpoints is JSON. Exceptions are endpoints returning binary data and oauth2-related endpoints.

## HTTP methods and headers

Following HTTP methods are used:

HTTP Method | Use case
----------- | --------
GET | Used for retreiving collection and objects. Various GET parameters will be available.
POST | Creating new objects. The data is posted as JSON object in the body.
DELETE | Deleting existing objects.
PATCH | Updating existing objects (partial update available) or triggering actions.

All responses have additionally following response headers:

Header | Type | Description | Example
------ | ---- | ----------- | -------
X-Request-Id | string | UUID. Can be used for support inquiries | c0ce64e5-d351-48fb-9c30-f19ffd3a2b0e
X-Ratelimit-Limit | int | The number of allowed requests in the current period | 1000
X-Ratelimit-Remaining | int | The number of remaining requests in the current period | 999

In case of support inquiries it is always optimal to pass the X-Request-ID value along with your request for faster identification of potential issues.

## HTTP response codes

As a restful API **we use HTTP Response codes for the basic information if a request was successful or not**. Every endpoint and action has the available success response codes documented and should be considered when implementing the API.
If a request fails, or any other information is available, the return body of the request will contain a JSON object with further information.

Following is a list of general failure response codes

Status code | Description | Notes
------ | ---- | -----------
400 | Bad Request | The request could not be understood by the server. Incoming parameters might not be valid.
401 | Unauthorized | The supplied Bearer token (if passed at all), is wrong or expired.
403 | Access denied | The authorized request is not allowed to access this resource / endpoint.
404 | Not found | The requested resource or endpoint does not exist.
405 | Method not allowed | The requested HTTP Method is not allowed for this endpoint.
406 | Not acceptable | The reques is not acceptable.
409 | Conflict | The request conflicts with the current state of the requested resource.
410 | Gone | The resource is no longer available.
415 | Unsupported media type | The requested or provided media type is currently not supported.
422 | Validation error | The provided data did not pass requirements as was rejected.
424 | Failed dependency | An external system required to execute the request was not available.
429 | Too many requests | The system is throttling due to too many requests in a given period.
500 | Server failure | The system is not acting as it should and an unexpected error happened.
503 | Service unavailable | We are either experiencing unexpected downtime, or are currently down for maintenance.

## Naming definitions

Following is an overview over certain terms and how we use them.

Name | Definition | Example
------ | ---- | -----------
Object | The smallest outputtable data part | A user with its attributes (Name, Surname, E-Mail etc).
Fields | An attribute or relationship of an object | email is an attribute of a user.
Relationships | Objects can have relationships to other objects ("to one" or "to many"). | A user has a "to many" relationship to associations. **Important:** Relationship names do not always match the entity type name.
Attributes | A specific attribute of an objects | email is an attribute of a user.
Collection | Multiple objects grouped into a response | Fetching a collection of documents and sorting/filtering by fields.
Entity type | Every object belongs to an entity type (always plural). | Users

## Throttling / Rate limiting

To ensure constant performance for all users, there is a limit of 300 requests / minute per user. If you receive a `429 Too many requests` http code, retry only after the specified waiting time in the response headers.

Following headers in the response will indicate when to retry your request.

Header | Type | Description
------ | ---- | -----------
X-Rate-Limit-Reset | int | The timestamp when the current period expires and the request can be retried.
Retry-After | int | The number of seconds you have to wait until you can retry (and the current period expires).

## Maintenance and temporary unavailability

In case of announced maintenance windows or short unexpected unavailabilities your request will receive a `503 Service unavailable` response code.
If you encounter this situation, please feel free to retry your API-call in a sensible interval, optimally implementing a 'back off strategy'.
An example of this would be to retry after 1 second, then 5, then 10, then 15 and so on...

# Authentication

<!-- ReDoc-Inject: <security-definitions> -->

## Introduction

 **IMPORTANT:** Following is a verbose detailed explanation of how the OAuth2 authorization flow works. If you already are familiar with how OAuth2 works, you already know how to use our API.

For all endpoints which require authentication you need to provide your access token in the header.

Header key | Value
---------- | --------
Authorization | Bearer YOURACCESSTOKEN

Following entities exist in the OAuth2 flow and are used in our API

Entity | Description
------ | --------
Authorization Grant | There are two different grant types (also called authorization types or grants) available. `Client credentials` and `Authorization code`.
Client (ID/Secret) | An entity that has to register itsself in the application. After registering a client, an ID-Secret pair is provided that is used for every authentication interaction with the API. **Important: Never expose your client secret to the public!**
Access token | This token is passed in the header of every request in the header key "Authorization". **Important: Only valid for 12 hours**
Refresh token | This token is received after successful authentication (only for Grant "Authorization Code") and does not expire. It can be used to generate new access tokens. The refresh token **can only be used once** to fetch a new access / refresh token pair. The newly received refresh tokens are then used for further calls.
Authorization code | The code that is exchanged for an access and refresh token in the grant type `Authorization code`. **Important: Only valid for 10 minutes**
Scopes | A scope is a defined part of the data/system. Access tokens are issued for one or multiple scopes and then can only access those parts of the system. Only ask for scopes you really need.

## Which grant type should i use?

You should choose the grant type `Client credentials`, if you would only like to access your own data of your own account. When creating a client, and choosing this grant type, your credentials will only enable you to access your data.

A typical usecase for the grant type `Client credentials` is if you are a programmer yourself, and would like to write a software that interacts with your own data in the application.

The Grant type `Authorization Code` is available for software developers that would like to integrate our API into their software and let other clients access their data, without having to hand over their private application credentials, as well as keep unlimited access (until revoked) via refresh tokens.

A typical usecase of the grant type `Authorization Code` would be a webshop-softwareprovider that lets their users connect their accounts to automatically trigger certain actions at certain events.
The software that is requesting access of a users data, leads the user to a login page of our application to grant access. When access is granted the initiating software receives further instructions how to obtain the required tokens.

## How to obtain a Client-ID
You can create as many client ids (every application / usecase should be separated by creating a separate client id) in your account.

Log in and navigate to your user profile and select `API Access`. You can create as many client applications as necessary.

## Scopes
When creating a Client-ID you define the maximum amount of scopes you will ask for when obtaining access tokens. You may ask for less, but never for more scopes than registered in your client.

If you do not ask for specific scopes when requesting access tokens, you will be given all scopes that your Client-ID as registered with.

Following scopes are currently available:

Scope | Description
------ | --------
letter | This scope allows you to send/upload letters as well as interact with them for all organisations that the user of the access token has permissions to.
ebill | This scope allows you to send/upload ebills as well as interact with them for all organisations that the user of the access token has permissions to.
email | This scope allows you to send/upload emails as well as interact with them for all organisations that the user of the access token has permissions to.
batch | This scope allows you to create/manage batches for all organisations that the user of the access token has permissions to.
webhook | This scope allows you to create/manage webhooks for all organisations that the user of the access token has permissions to.
organisation_read | This scope allows you to fetch information about which organisations the user is currently active in and their details.

## Use Client credentials grant

To obtain the access token required for making an API call you need to make following HTTP request

POST /auth/access-tokens\
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

Form field | Value
------ | --------
grant_type | client_credentials
client_id | Your client id (see [here](#section/Authentication/How-to-obtain-a-Client-ID) how to obtain)
client_secret | Your client secret you obtained
scope (optional) | Required scope(s) (multiple separated by space)

```
Example:

curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=client_credentials" \
--data-urlencode "client_id=INSERT_YOUR_CLIENT_ID" \
--data-urlencode "client_secret=INSERT_YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET" \
--data-urlencode "scope=INSERT_YOUR_SCOPES_HERE" \
https://identity.pingen.com/auth/access-tokens
```

If successful, this will return the access token and validity period.

```
{
"token_type":"Bearer",
"expires_in":43200,
"access_token":"YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
}
```

This access token can now be used to make API-Requests, and is passed as header value. When the token expires, a new access token should be generated in the same manner.

## Use Authorization Code grant

The process of retrieving the access and refresh token from a user is interactive. The user who wants to provide access to his account, will have to follow through an authorization process that in the end will deliver a refresh and access token to the initiator/software provider/client.

This process contains two steps:
 * Step 1) The initiating software leads the user to be prompted for access.
 * Step 2) If access is granted by the user, the initiating software exchanges an authorization code for tokens.

### Step 1) Initiating the authorization

The initiating software needs to redirect the user (optionally via popup) to pingen in order for the user to approve and authorize the request. The URL is constructed from following elements:

GET /auth/authorize

URL Parameter | Value
------------- | --------
response_type | code
state | Randomly generated string that will be returned after the user has authenticated himself.
code_challenge | Randomly generated alphanumerical string (exactly 43 characters) that will be returned at the end of the process with the access and refresh token. It serves the purpose to authenticate the response from the server.
client_id | The client id of the application provider (see [here](#section/Authentication/How-to-obtain-a-Client-ID) how to obtain)
redirect_uri | The URL that will receive the authorization code. Has to be identical to the one that was entered when registering the client.
scope (optional) | Required scope(s) (multiple separated by space)

```
Example:

https://identity.pingen.com/auth/authorize?response_type=code&state=RANDOMGENERATEDSTRING&code_challenge=RANDOMGENERATEDSTRING&client_id=YOURCLIENTID&redirect_uri=YOURREDIRECTURI&scope=letter
```

The user will be prompted to login with his credentials, and grant access to the requesting application.

### Step 2) Exchanging the code for tokens

Upon user granting access, the browser will redirect the user to the provided redirect_uri including following GET parameters:

GET Parameter | Value
------------- | --------
code | This is your Authorization code to be used further below (**Important**: Only valid for 10 minutes)
state | The state value you passed in Step 1)

```
Example:

GET https://YOURREDIRECTURL/?code=AUTHORIZATIONCODE&state=YOUR_PREVIOUSLY_PASSED_STATE
```
Verify that the state parameter has the same value as the value you initiated the process in Step 1). If these values do not match then cancel any further proceedings, as this means that probably the request was a fraudulent one.

Now you can fetch the access- and refresh-token making the following POST-Request:

POST /auth/access-tokens\
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

Form field | Value
------ | --------
grant_type | authorization_code
client_id | Your client id (see [here](#section/Authentication/How-to-obtain-a-Client-ID) how to obtain)
client_secret | Your client secret you obtained
redirect_uri | Your redirect URL
code | The authorization code you received
code_verifier | The code challenge you generated in Step 1)
scope (optional) | The scope(s) passed in Step 1)

```
Example:

curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=authorization_code" \
--data-urlencode "client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID" \
--data-urlencode "client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET" \
--data-urlencode "redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI" \
--data-urlencode "code=CODE_YOU_RECEIVED" \
--data-urlencode "code_verifier=CODE_CHALLENGE_THAT_YOU_GENERATED" \
--data-urlencode "scope=YOUR_REQUESTED_SCOPES" \
https://identity.pingen.com/auth/access-tokens
```

If successful, this will return the access and refresh token as well as the validity period.

```
{
"token_type":"Bearer",
"expires_in":43200,
"access_token":"ACCESS_TOKEN_OF_USER",
"refresh_token":"REFRESH_TOKEN_FOR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
}
```

You can immediately use this access token to make any API-Request on behalf of the user. If you would like to be able to make API requests after the access token has expired, you need to store the refresh token in your database / permanent storage.

To get a new access token (and refresh token) for the user, you can make the following request using the stored refresh token

POST /auth/access-tokens\
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

Form field | Value
------ | --------
grant_type | refresh_token
client_id | Your client id (see [here](#section/Authentication/How-to-obtain-a-Client-ID) how to obtain)
client_secret | Your client secret you obtained
refresh_token | The refresh token you stored for that user

```
Example:

curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=refresh_token" \
--data-urlencode "client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID" \
--data-urlencode "client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET" \
--data-urlencode "refresh_token=YOUR_STORED_REFRESH_TOKEN_OF_USER" \
https://identity.pingen.com/auth/access-tokens
```

This will return you a new access token for the user:

```
{
"token_type":"Bearer",
"expires_in":43200,
"access_token":"ACCESS_TOKEN_OF_USER",
"refresh_token":"NEW_REFRESH_TOKEN_OF_USER_THAT_YOU_HAVE_TO_STORE"
}
```

 **IMPORTANT:** When using the refresh token for fetching new access tokens, the refresh token used is automatically revoked, and you will have to store the new refresh token received for the next time you want to fetch a new access token.

# Advanced

## Idempotency

Idempotency means that when repeating a certain API call, the system state does not change (and for example cause duplication or other unwanted effects).
By definition `GET` and `DELETE` calls are idempotent and can be retried without risk.

If however due to network interruptions/timeout `PATCH` or `POST` API calls do not produce a result and are retried, they will either cause duplication or other unwanted effects as it is possible that the previous request indeed reach our systems and was processed.

To be able to safely retry these kind of API calls, you can set the HTTP Header `Idempotency-Key` with any unique 1-64 character string (we suggest UUID v4) for any `POST` or `PATCH` request. If the API call is retried make sure that the same key is used as for the initial request.

If indeed the initial API call was successful, but just the response did not reach your server, any subsequent API calls with the same Idempotency-Key will receive the same HTTP code and content as the first API call.

You can determine if an idempotent API call was replayed by inspecting the `Idempotent-Replayed` header for the value `true`.

Idempotency keys and their result are cached for 24 hours. After this period the keys are free to be used again and will not prevent a duplicate request.

If a subsequent request with the same Idempotency key is made while the first request is still in progress, you will receive an error (conflict). It is therefore recommended to have a sensible delay of at least a few seconds before retrying.

## Sorting collections

The GET Parameter `sort` accepts a string representing the sorting expression.

Following are a few examples:

Desired sorting | Value of parameter `sort`
--------------- | --------
name ASC | name
name DESC | -name
surname DESC, name ASC | -surname,name

## Filtering collections

The GET Parameter `filter` accepts a JSON representing the filtering expression.

Assuming you would like to filter a collection and only receive entries where the attribute "exampleattribute" equals to "filtervalue" your expression would be:

```
{
"exampleattribute":"filtervalue"
}
```

You can combine multiple expressions. For example getting a collection of objects where the attribute "exampleattribute" equals to "filtervalue", and the "additionalattribute" equals to 120 your expression would be:

```
{
"and":[
{"exampleattribute":"filtervalue"},
{"additionalattribute":120}
]
}
```

More complex combinations are also possible: (key1=a AND key2=b) OR key3=c

```
{
"or":[
{
"and":[
{"key1":"a"},
{"key2":"b"}
]
},
{"key3":"c"}
]
}
```

Another example: key1="a" AND (key2="b" OR key3="c")

```
{
"and":[
{"key1":"a"},
{
"or":[
{"key2":"b"},
{"key3":"c"}
]
}
]
}
```

And a last example: key1="a" AND (key2="b" OR (key3="c" AND key4="d"))

```
{
"and":[
{"key1":"a"},
{
"or":[
{"key2":"b"},
{
"and":[
{"key3":"c"},
{"key4":"d"}
]
}
]
}
]
}
```

Comparators can also be different to equaling. Following comparators are available, **and are prepended to the value to be searched** (not all comparators are available for all value types)

Comparator | Meaning
---------- | --------
< | smaller than
<= | smaller or equals than
> | greater than
>= | greater or equals than
! | not equals to
~ | approximately

## Searching collections

Plain blind searches can be done by passing the string to be searched in the parameter `q`

It is possible to pass characters, words or sentences in this parameter, and the API will try to deliver the most relevant results.

## Paginating collections

Every collection endpoint accepts the two parameters `page[number]` and `page[limit]`. The default limit 20, the maximum is 100 objects per page.

Using them together enables you to do simple paging. In every collection response you will furthermore receive the full URLs of the previous, next and last page (if available).

## Sparse fieldsets

By default the API will return all available attributes and relationships for all objects in the response (while retrieving collections and getting objects)

If you do not require all fields of the objects you can specify exactly which fields you require by specifying them comma separated in the `fields[TYPE]` query parameter (also for included related objects). When acquiring large sets of data, and requiring only few fields, this can improve response times and network traffic.

```
Example:

curl -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer YOURACCESSTOKEN" \
https://api.pingen.com/user?fields[users]=email,first_name,last_name
```

## Including relationships

To avoid having to make multiple roundtrips to get child objects, they can be included in the response without making a separate API call. This only is available for 'to one' relationships.
This is possible for both getting collections and objects.

```
Example:

curl -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer YOURACCESSTOKEN" \
https://api.pingen.com/user/associations?include=organisation
```
# Simulation

Any document sent on our staging environment is NOT really delivered. It is therefore safe to try any API call.

In production, a document (as an example a letter) goes through various stages including analysis, transferring to our printcenters, getting responses about undeliverability and so on.
For many developers it is important to test the flow in case of failure, returned letters etc. To provide this possibility we have activated various scenarios on staging that can be triggered by using a specific filename to simulate different lifecycles of a letter.

Filename (letters) | Effect
--------------- | --------
 *_simulate_undeliverable.pdf | Simulates the lifecycle of a letter until it is marked as undeliverable.
 *_simulate_unprintable.pdf | Simulates the lifecycle of a letter that passed our inspections, but was rejected by our print centers for unknown reasons.
 *_simulate_cancellable.pdf | Stops the lifecycle of a letter in a status, where it still can be cancelled.
Any other filename | Simulates the lifecycle of a letter until it was been delivered to the distributor and considered sent.

Filename (ebills) | Effect
--------------- | --------
 *_simulate_refused.pdf | Simulates the lifecycle of an ebill that was refused by the recipient.
 *_simulate_approved.pdf | Simulates the lifecycle of an ebill that was approved, but not yet paid by the recipient.
 *_simulate_paid.pdf | Simulates the lifecycle of an ebill that was approved and subsequently paid.
 *_simulate_cancellable.pdf | Stops the lifecycle of an ebill in a status, where it still can be cancelled.
Any other filename | Simulates the lifecycle of a letter until it was been delivered to the distributor and considered sent.

	"github.com/pingencom/pingen2-sdk-go/batches"
	"github.com/pingencom/pingen2-sdk-go/oauth"
)

func main() {
    config, _ := pingen2sdk.InitSDK(
        "clientId",
        "clientSecret",
        "staging",
    )

    params := map[string]string{
        "grant_type": "client_credentials",
        "scope":      "letter batch webhook organisation_read user",
    }

    tokenResp, err := oauth.GetToken(config, params)
    accessToken := tokenResp["access_token"].(string)
    
    apiRequestor := api.NewAPIRequestor(accessToken, config)

    batchClient := batches.NewBatches("organisationID", apiRequestor)

    splitSize := 5
    splitPos := batches.SplitPositionFirstPage
    separator := "comma"

    resp, err := batchClient.UploadAndCreateBatch(
        "test.zip",
        "Test Upload Batch",
        batches.IconRocket,
        "test.zip",
        batches.AddressPositionLeft,
        batches.GroupingTypeZip,
        batches.SplitTypeFile,

        &separator,
        &splitPos,

    'Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json',

tags.description:
Pingen can make an HTTP POST request to a webhook URL when specific events occure.

### Expected response
If your webhook responds with a HTTP 2xx code it will determine the webhook call is successful and will not retry.
For any other HTTP code, we will retry the request based on a fixed retry-schedule.

### Retry schedule
1 minute, 5 minutes, 10 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours. After that time the request failed and there are no more attempts.

### Security
To verify the authenticity of the request, we send an HTTP Header 'Signature' which you need to compare
to the signature you calculate using the below formula:

### PHP example:
```
// payload is the full json that you received in the request
// secret is the string you defined when configuring the webhook

$signature = hash_hmac('sha256', $payload, $secret);
```

### Python example:
```
import hmac
import hashlib


hash = hmac.new(b'secret', b'payload', hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
```

### Node.js example:
```
// IMPORTANT payload from response should be unchanged.

const crypto = require('crypto');

let hmac = crypto.createHmac('sha256', 'secret');
let signed = hmac.update(String.raw`payload`).digest('hex');
```
